book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Brat is locked in after a scalding

indicators.note: locked in means held inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of after, the word a, and the start of scalding

explanation.surface: A naughty child is shut away after a severe burn.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across three words: aftER A SCALding.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous child, much the same as a brat.

clue.text: Alliance broken by unruly mob

indicators.note: something broken has fallen to pieces, so the letters are put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political pact is shattered by a rioting crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaille is a French loanword, rare in English; the anagram fodder is the whole first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaille is a contemptuous word for the common rabble, from French for a pack of dogs.

clue.text: Groups of actors supporting wide screens

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so the actors come after the other part

parts.note: broad means wide
a cast is the group of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Several troupes of performers are backing a widescreen film release.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' means placed beneath, so the actors' word comes second. Screens here is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to show it on television, which is to broadcast it, here in the verb's third person.

clue.text: Fish develop acne, maybe once!

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters of the skin complaint are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish breaks out in spots, as might have happened long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' tells you the definition is old-fashioned: perchance is an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an archaic word for perhaps, so maybe as it was said in former times.

clue.text: Fit a bell outside front of entrance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: outside means only the outer letters at each end of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of bell

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of entrance

explanation.surface: Install a doorbell outside, by the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a doorbell; really the bell is reduced to its two outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fit for a task is to be able or capable, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Smoking gun found in fast car

parts.note: something smoking is very hot
rod is American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Damning evidence turns up inside a sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: A smoking gun is proof of guilt, a phrase that hides two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for extra speed and acceleration.

clue.text: Ancient clock parts need workers with experience

parts.note: ancient means very old
a clock face has hands

explanation.surface: Repairing an antique clock needs skilled craftsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands are both clock pointers and workers, so the second piece doubles the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hands are veterans who have long practice at a job, so they are experienced workers.

clue.text: Andrew was warned to set an example

definitions.text: Andrew was warned to set an example

parts.note: surface reading: a man called Andrew was given a warning
setter's reading: the name Andrew is the word warned with its letters set in a new order, so it is a specimen of a kind of wordplay

explanation.surface: Andrew is told off so that others will learn from his punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew and warned use the same six letters, so 'Andrew was warned' before being rearranged; 'set' is a cue for rearranging letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging the letters of another is the term for this device, and Andrew/warned is a textbook specimen of it.

clue.text: Mostly intended to be stingy

indicators.note: mostly signals not quite all, so the word for intended is cut short at its end

parts.note: a past-tense synonym of intended, as in 'I meant to'

explanation.surface: Someone largely set out to be tight with money.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T of MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean is the everyday British word for ungenerous with money, a synonym of stingy.

clue.text: Involve compiler coming back to grill in America

indicators.note: something coming back travels the other way, so the compiler's word is read right to left

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to themself as me
broil is the American word for grilling

explanation.surface: The setter returns to cook on a barbecue in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of a crossword is often called the compiler and stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict or difficulty, so involve is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A financial institution rumoured to be after daily transport

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in each day, also called a char

indicators.note: what is rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so only the sound of these words matters

parts.note: a bank, spoken, matches the second half of the coach name

explanation.surface: A bank is said to be coming after the daily commuter service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily transport' looks like a commuter train, but daily is the cleaner, CHAR. 'After' places the bank sound behind her.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings, a form of road transport.

clue.text: Clear the surrounding ground

indicators.note: the two words before it are surrounding the answer, holding its letters within them

parts.note: runs from the second letter of the first word through the start of the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear away everything on the land round about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear the surrounding ground' reads as a gardening job; the letters sit inside clEAR THe.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is soil, the material of the land underfoot, a direct synonym for ground.

clue.text: Ring back about unique tree

indicators.note: going back means reading the word for ring from its end to its start
about means placed around, so the reversed word wraps the single letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
unique means one of a kind, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A call is returned regarding a rare and special tree.
explanation.walkthrough: LLAC goes around I to make LILAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a small flowering tree or shrub with scented purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Leave, if there's a group performing

parts.note: taken as written
a band is a group of musicians
a performer is on when they are on stage

explanation.surface: You might walk out of a venue when a band is playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A band on' run together reads as one seven-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a place or person is to desert them, so it matches leave used as a verb.

clue.text: A cheap Tory trick from a drug dealer

indicators.note: a trick deceives, so the letters before it are disguised by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written, the article and two words together

explanation.surface: A shabby Conservative political stunt is traced to a narcotics pusher.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'Acheap' is a scanning slip for 'A cheap'. Drug dealer sounds criminal, but it is the old word for a chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was a pharmacist who prepared and sold medicines, so literally a dealer in drugs.

clue.text: Loud teenager running wild — a type with no responsibilities

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: running wild means out of control and disordered, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy adolescent out of control is the sort who answers to no one.
explanation.walkthrough: F is from musical notation (forte).
explanation.definitionFit: A free agent is someone not bound to any employer or obligation, able to act independently.

clue.text: Chefs with stress find they help

definitions.text: Chefs with stress find they help

parts.note: surface reading: cooks under strain in a busy kitchen
setter's reading: the stress is physical force, steam held at high force inside sealed pans that speed the cooking

explanation.surface: Overworked cooks discover that some kitchen gadget eases their load.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress is read as mental strain, but in physics it is force per area, the thing these sealed pans build up.
explanation.definitionFit: These sealed pans cook food quickly with steam held under raised force, so they help busy cooks.

clue.text: Buy a grip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to acquire something by paying, the verb
second meaning: a firm hold or leverage, the noun

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'agrip' is a scanning slip for 'a grip'. The second sense, a firm foothold, is less familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the formal verb for buying, and as a noun it means a firm hold giving leverage.

clue.text: Forceful characters in the camp welcome one

indicators.note: characters in the phrase means its letters, used freely in any order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Strong personalities at the camp greet a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcome' means the camp letters take in the I before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means expressed with force and clarity, as in an emphatic denial.

clue.text: Right, that's covered the mail with a quick reply!

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: something covered has a layer around it, so the word for that's surrounds the mail word

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
the post is the mail service

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off a sharp answer by return of post.
explanation.walkthrough: i.e. stands for Latin id est, 'that is', so "that's" gives those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, originally a fencer's swift counter-thrust.

clue.text: Enquire closely about worker in store

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the enquiry word goes around the insect

parts.note: to pry is to enquire too closely
a worker ant, the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: Questioning someone closely about an employee in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Store looks like a shop, but it is a place where food is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where food is kept, a kitchen storeroom.

clue.text: Oriental jumps around with expectations

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the jumps word is placed on both sides of the single letter

parts.note: hops are small jumps
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: An Asian athlete leaps about, full of expectation.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriental gives E for east, as in crosswords generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes are things one expects or wishes to happen, so the plural noun matches expectations.

clue.text: Split if one's married after school?

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
one is I, so one's reads as I is
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A couple wonders whether to separate if one of them weds after leaving school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After school' puts SCH first; 'if' is filler for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division, especially within a church or organisation.

clue.text: Arrest the second highest

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
the top is the highest point

explanation.surface: Police detain the man ranked number two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The second highest' sounds like a ranking, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a process is to halt it, so the verb matches in its sense of bringing to a halt.

clue.text: Suggestions of strikes about direction

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for strikes encloses the compass letter

parts.note: hits are blows or strikes
N for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Talk of industrial walkouts circles around the question of leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' suggests industrial action, but here they are blows; direction is any compass point, here N.
explanation.definitionFit: Hints are indirect suggestions or clues, so the plural nouns match exactly.

clue.text: Fat little girl with tiny top

parts.note: Sue is a short girl's name

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of tiny

explanation.surface: A plump young girl wearing a skimpy top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little girl' is a short girl's name, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is hard animal fat used in cooking puddings and pastry.

clue.text: To avoid charges at function?

parts.note: surface reading: escaping a fee or a criminal accusation
setter's reading: a function is a party, and the charge avoided is the ticket price, by getting in uninvited

explanation.surface: Someone tries to dodge a fee, or prosecution, at some formal event.
explanation.walkthrough: Charges suggest the police, but they are entry fees, and a function here is a party or reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to attend a party or event without an invitation, thus without paying.

clue.text: One might make nurse go to work!

definitions.text: One might make nurse go to work!

parts.words: One might make nurse go to work
parts.note: surface reading: a boss forcing a reluctant nurse to start a shift
setter's reading: in an operating theatre, a doctor sets the nursing staff working by starting the operation

explanation.surface: Someone orders a reluctant nurse off to her shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase hints at shuffling the letters of nurse, a tempting false path, but it is a plain picture of the theatre team.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon leads an operation, and theatre nurses work under the operating doctor's direction.

clue.text: Groups celebrating leave one with mess inside

parts.note: to part is to leave or go away
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: inside means only the interior letters of the word are kept, dropping its first and last

parts.note: the middle two letters of mess

explanation.surface: Revellers leave someone behind with chaos left inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess inside' looks like disorder within, but it means the inner letters of the word mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties are social gatherings held to celebrate, so groups celebrating describes them.
